title: Raise a corded mini blind hand over hand until its bottom rail is level with a tape mark, and let its cord lock hold it
instruction: Raise the blind until its bottom rail is level with the blue tape, and leave it there.
context: Raising a corded mini blind by its pull cord is a chore most people have done. The maker's instructions (Levolor, stock metal blinds): "To raise or lower the installed blind, pull the cords to the LEFT (Fig. I) to disengage. Gently raise or lower to desired position." "To lock blind into desired position, pull the cords to the RIGHT (Fig. J)." The lock is at the right end: a cord let go hanging straight or to the right is caught; let go while pulled toward the centre, the blind runs down. Here a 3 mm cord hangs free in front of the slats; 30 cm of rise is more cord than one stroke within reach gives (the cord can be held 44 to 14 cm above the table), so it is pulled hand over hand, one hand keeping it taut while the other takes a new grip higher up, or in strokes with the lock catching between them. The rail gathers the slats as it rises and must stop within 2 cm of the tape; then the cord is let go so the lock holds.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y left, heights above the table. Wall section (painted plywood, fixed): face at x 29, 11 cm deep, y -36 to 66, 90 tall; window opening y -14.5 to 44.5, 2 to 52 up; sill board 2 tall, 2 proud of the face; pane at x 39. Blind (white 1 in aluminium, corded, 22.5 in wide, shortened to 20 slats), inside the opening, fully lowered: steel headrail 57.2 x 3.5 x 2.5 (x 30-33.5, 49.5-52 up); 20 slats 56.6 x 2.5 cm, 8 g, 2.2 cm apart; steel bottom rail 57 x 2.5 x 1 cm, 100 g, underside 3 up; tilt wand at the left end. Pull cord: leaves the lock at x 29.8, y -7, 49.3 up and hangs 17.5 cm, white tassel 1.2 cm across, 3.6 long on an 8 mm stem, 27.4 to 31.8 up. Blue painter's tape on the wall face, y -21.5 to -15, 1.2 tall, centred 33 up. Arms at the ready pose. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: 0 if the blind ever runs down: the rail falls 4 cm or more within 0.5 s (latched; video). Else at the end, with the cord let go (no finger within 15 mm of cord or tassel) and the rail still (under 2 mm) for the last 5 s: 1.0 if the rail's underside is within 2 cm of the tape's centre line (tape measure from the table); 0.5 if it is elsewhere but at least 5 cm above its start. Otherwise 0.
reset_notes: Lower the blind fully: pull the cord to the left (toward the centre) to free the lock and let it run up slowly until the rail rests 1 cm above the sill, then let the cord hang straight and still. Slats level (tilt open). Arms at the ready pose. Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: PhysX articulation. Cord: a rigid top length on a ball joint at the lock with a pay-out slide (its upper part hidden in the wall), nine 15 mm lengths on ball joints and the tassel. A mimic joint couples pay-out 1:1 to the rail's slide: the lift cords over the headrail. Slats slide, stop at their ladder rungs and stack on the rising rail. The lock is a rule: a one-way stop (8 mm catch) unless the cord is 15 deg toward the centre. No tilt.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both arms drew back toward their bases and stayed there, never touching the cord; the blind stayed down); demo: 1.0
